core_memory.user_family_description: My family is supportive, close-knit, and lively. They show me unconditional love through their interactions with Archie. Even with a busy schedule, I know I'm always welcome at home, where I can recharge and find comfort. Archie's enthusiasm when I return home is a highlight of my day.
core_memory.friendship_story_short: I've formed strong bonds with my closest friends at college. They've become like a second family to me. These friendships have made the stresses and workload of being a CS major manageable.

archival_memory.graduation_story_short: As a fourth-year, graduation is looming, and I'm excited about the future. However, I'm also dreading the day when all these friends I've made scatter to different corners of the world. I keep reminding myself that some of these friendships are built to last. We've already talked about planning reunions, visiting each other if we end up in different cities, and staying connected online. It's weird thinking how we'll be grown adults in different jobs, possibly different time zones, but hopefully still able to maintain the bond we forged here.
archival_memory.transcending_distance_story: I believe real friendship is about having a strong sense of trust, loyalty, and empathy that can transcend distance. I've seen that with Tony, who's interning across the country this semester, yet we still FaceTime regularly. I see the same dedication in others, like Carla, who's applying to master's programs abroad. We promised that if either of us ends up in Europe, the other has to come visit.
archival_memory.gratitude_story: I'm extremely grateful for the friendships I've made through sailing, the gym, gaming, research, random campus encounters—everything. They're truly an integral part of my college experience, reminding me that there's more to this journey than racking up achievements on my resume. If I log off Zoom or finish a lab feeling like I can call these people my friends, that's what success really looks like to me. And I know that no matter where I end up in my career, I'll carry a piece of each of these friends with me. Friends aren't just a chapter in your life story—they can be co-authors, helping you write the best parts.
